label: What the Guide Me Builder's Export puts in the zip: file names, the ready Guide me code and the read-me

params.name: module_js
readme
params.default:
# Guide me - {title}

A live, step-by-step tour of the page "{page}" on {portal}: a soft veil, a spotlight on each part, one card with a picture, the narration, Back / Next, Listen (the browser's own free voice) and Close.

## What is in this folder

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `{module_file}` | Ready to use: adds a Guide me button and opens the tour |
| `{script_file}` | The tour itself (a Guide Me script, format {format}) - plain text anyone can read and edit |
| `guide-kit.js` | The kit that draws the tour |
| `guide-kit.css` | Its look (takes your site's colours when it has --brand / --panel / --ink tokens) |
| `icons.js` | The icons the cards use |

## On one of our own portals

Do not copy the code. Open How to Use -> Configure for the page "{page}", choose Guide me, import `{script_file}` and Save. The portal already carries the kit.

## On any other site

1. Copy this whole folder next to the page (all five files stay together).
2. Add, anywhere in the page:

```html
<script type="module">import { mountGuideMe } from './{module_file}'; mountGuideMe();</script>
```

A Guide me button appears at the bottom right. To use a button of your own instead, give it the attribute `data-guide-me` - mountGuideMe wires it and adds nothing.

The spotlight finds each part by the selectors in the script (`target`). Give the page's parts matching `id` or `data-tour` attributes so every step lands on its part; a part that is not on screen gets a centred card instead.

description_nl: Skill guide-me-script section 4. module_js and readme are templates: {page} {portal} {title} {format} {module_file} {script_file}, and {page_json} {script_json} {words_json} (chip ui.guide + the road names of ui.shell) {settings_json} (chip guide.settings) {button_label_json} (ui.guide guide_me) {button_style_json} are filled with the values written as code. Only a {name} with no space after the brace is filled, so the code's own braces stay as written. kit_files are copied from the portal's own kit (core/static).
weight_basis: The exported code and words. Edit them here, never in Python.
